results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 33 prose units' summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs p01-p33 in spec order; the five introduction callouts (IN THIS CHAPTER, WHY THE BUSINESS CARES, WHY ARCHITECTS SHOULD CARE, KEY POINTS, FAILURE PATTERNS) match no spec paragraph and carry the roadmap and thesis-statement placement the spec names.

Units marked two_ideas each hold one controlling idea: the KEY POINTS callout is the declared three-bullet thesis statement; Glance ¶2 is one reading of the glance table (margin as context, last row as the point) exactly as p05 declares; Volumes ¶2 is announced as 'Two caveats on reading it'; Worked Examples ¶3 gives the role of each of the other four stories (p27); How the Chapters Use Veldmark ¶1 is a lead-in to its problem-to-chapter table (p29); the two conclusion paragraphs carry synthesis-with-callback and so-what-with-hand-off as p32 and p33 declare.

Every paragraph ties to a supporting claim: introduction and people/chapters to MV1, glance/brands/volumes to MV2, history/systems and glance ¶2 to MV3, problems and bike/Golf examples to MV4, Common Ground to MV5; no orphan paragraph.

Tables, figures and examples are explained: the glance table by Glance ¶2, the history table by 'Each phase left a layer', the brand table by the revenue-share sentence and Figure 1's caption, the systems table and Figure 2 by 'Three facts', the cast table by its lead-in on legitimate goals, Figures 3-5 by captions, the decision table by its lead-in and Figure 5's caption, the worked-examples table by the bike and Golf paragraphs, the problem-to-chapter table by its lead-in, and the bike scenario by 'what a successful classifieds platform looks like after twenty years of reasonable local decisions'.

results.draft_locus: Volumes Every Design Is Sized Against ¶2
results.quote: And ratios matter more than totals: Tradeyard Netherlands and Portugal have almost the same monthly users per live listing (2.3 and 2.5), yet a new Dutch listing gets its first contact in a median of 2.6 hours and a Portuguese one in 19. [[liquidity-and-network-effects]] explains why
results.finding: The statistic is not followed by a sentence saying what it shows. The spec says it shows that similar totals hide different liquidity; the draft frames it as 'ratios matter more than totals' and then gives an example in which the ratio is the same and the outcome differs, and defers the explanation to another chapter. Flow reader A (A5) could not tell what lesson the sentence was meant to give.

All other boundaries express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information, e.g. 'That duplication comes from a history' (cause_effect), 'Veldmark Ads is the exception' (contrast), 'Two caveats on reading it' (contrast), 'These brands and systems have owners' (elaboration), 'When Ingrid arrives' (time), 'Veldmark's answer to these problems' (problem_solution), 'In its chapters, the Golf plays the same role' (similarity), 'Smaller stories' (contrast), 'The three preface pages make one argument' (conclusion_summary).

results.draft_locus: From the Preface to Part I ¶2
results.quote: So every chapter's opening scene is one more view of a group you already know, and each chapter explains a decision about a boundary, not a product choice.
results.finding: Declared cause_effect, carrying over 'the one argument at three sizes'. The 'So' follows the callback sentence about the general-manager scene, from which neither the 'group you already know' nor the 'decision about a boundary' follows; the link to 'loses matches at its boundaries' at the start of ¶1 is not picked up. Both flow readers (A12, B12) report that the 'So' does not follow.

Both flow readers describe the declared organisation: a large-to-small portrait (glance, history, brands, volumes, systems, people) in prerequisite order, then problems followed by the Common Ground answer (problem_solution), then worked examples and how chapters use the group. Neither marks any section's position unclear; both say no section needs to move. Points dismissed as not material for this audience: the opening reference to the previous page (A1, B2) and the unglossed pattern names (A7, B6) and general-manager scene (A11) are in audience.already_knows; dense table cells (A2, A3) and callout forward references (B1, B3) were resolved without losing the thread.

results.draft_locus: From the Preface to Part I ¶2
results.quote: So every chapter's opening scene is one more view of a group you already know, and each chapter explains a decision about a boundary, not a product choice.
results.finding: Reader A (A12): 'The "So" does not follow from the previous paragraph. The second clause (boundary versus product choice) is a new claim that the page has not set up.' The spec's order is fine; the prose does not connect the so-what to the synthesis's 'loses matches at its boundaries' and 'share platforms, not products'.
results.corroborated_by: flow-b, item B12: 'The "So" does not follow from the previous paragraph ... The claim "a decision about a boundary, not a product choice" is new here and was not prepared anywhere on the page.'

results.quote: The dated decisions the chapters rely on, by year (Figure 5's four plateaus):
results.finding: Reader A (A8): 'The table is also introduced through Figure 5's plateaus, yet the figure comes after the table, and the table is ordered by date rather than grouped into plateaus. The plateau names ... appear only in the caption. I had to scroll past the table to understand the reference.' A placement and wording problem in the prose (define the plateaus in the lead-in or place Figure 5 first).
results.corroborated_by: flow-b, item B8: 'The sentence refers to Figure 5 and its "four plateaus" before the figure appears, and the plateaus ... are defined only in the caption after the table.'

results.quote: Single listings show the problems and the program's decisions best. Five stories recur throughout the book. Their facts never change, so a reader can follow one listing across many chapters.
results.finding: Reader A (A9): 'Two of the five examples are not single listings. The Barcelona ring is 180 listings from 26 accounts, and the Sunday-evening brown-out is a platform incident. The framing sentence does not match the table that follows.' The spec declares this framing (section transition 'introduces: Single listings that show them'; p25 'follow one listing'), so the inaccuracy originates in the spec.
results.corroborated_by: flow-b, item B9: 'Two of the five stories are not single listings ... I had to adjust the frame partway through the table.'

results.quote: a messaging check that ran after delivery, a rule that reached Belgium three days late, an analytics extract that recorded the sale as "expired", and a digest that never asked whether the bike was still for sale. Six months later, Femke's erasure request finds **seven** copies of the listing.
results.finding: Reader A (A10): 'Several of these facts are not in the bike row just above ... The paragraph presents itself as a summary of the example but adds new facts.' Right after the table is presented as facts that 'never change', the paragraph introduces new ones without saying they are what the chapters go on to reveal; the Belgium rule connects only to the opening callout.
results.corroborated_by: flow-b, item B10: 'The Rotterdam-bike paragraph after the table introduces facts that are not in the "core facts" row ... I went back to check whether I had missed these.'

results.quote: Four identity systems, four trust-and-safety stacks, three search engines, three clouds, four product catalogs, three data warehouses.
results.finding: Reader B (B4): the counts in 'four of everything' do not match the systems table (three trust-and-safety entries and a dash for Keybridge, identity entries countable as four to six, four data rows, no product catalogs at all), so a reader checking the claim against the table 'finds no clean match'. On a reference page meant for checking figures this is material.

results.quote: None of these is a technology problem alone.
results.finding: Reader B (B7): Figure 3, which shows only problem 1, sits between the eight-problem list and this commentary, so 'these' is cut off from the list: 'I had to look back up to see what "these" meant.'

results.quote: chairs the architecture advice forum (set up April 2027)
results.finding: The architecture advice forum is used in Ingrid's row of the cast table before the page says what it is; it is explained only in The Common Ground Program ¶3 ('a weekly, open meeting that gives advice rather than approvals'). Reader A (A6) paused on it as a forward reference.
results.corroborated_by: flow-b, item B5: 'Ingrid "chairs the architecture advice forum (set up April 2027)". The forum is explained only in the Common Ground section.'

results.finding: The introduction opens with a direct statement of why the book uses one detailed fictional group and why the alternatives fail; it is not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary definition, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', does not merely restate the thesis, holds no body evidence, and is not a grab bag; it synthesises the three preface pages, calls back to the introduction and hands off to Part I. The 'boundary, not a product choice' clause is the spec's declared so-what derived from 'loses matches at its boundaries' and 'share platforms, not products'; its weak connection is recorded under transitions and flow.

¶1 states what no single section states: the three preface pages are one argument at three sizes (liquidity machine, fifteen ways of losing matches at boundaries, Veldmark's problems as instances with Common Ground as the claim written as a program). ¶2 gives the so-what: each chapter's scene is one more view of a known group and explains a decision about a boundary.

Returns to the introduction's general-manager scene as declared: 'the six minutes to searchable is Veldmark's problem 2, and the sold bike in Tuesday's alert e-mails is Femke's €240 city bike in 214 of them.'

The intro reader predicted the roadmap's five promises in order (glance and history; brands and volumes; systems and people; eight problems and Common Ground; worked examples and how chapters use them) plus the close on the preface, the kind of evidence (invented but consistent figures, tables, named systems and people, short scenes, real companies kept separate) and the declarative reference tone.

The reader named five problems with their patterns, all agreeing with the expected answer: Four of everything (Deal-Shaped Architecture), Six weeks for a category (Category Straitjacket, Attribute Junkyard), Duplicates at Hearthly (Seeing Double), Payment-link phishing (Fast Mail for Fraudsters), Overlap in Poland (Deal-Shaped Architecture), and correctly noted the unlabelled three.
The reader confirmed €225 and Monday 8 March 2027, corrected the buyer fee to €11.95 (5% × €225 + €0.70) and the reservation time to 14:02, exactly as expected.
